This position administers a defined operational program involving budgetary and financial management, payroll, space planning, student services, human resources, communications, and informational technology functions, along with purchasing, event support, and contracts and grants support, including administrative and event support for research development and workforce training programs, and supervises a small staff of student assistants. This position gathers and analyzes financial and human resources data, prepares reports and analyses of financial and HR operational activities, evaluates current and proposed services, and assists in drafting organizational website and newsletter content and correspondence to organizational constituents. This position functions as a resource on complex financial discrepancies and vendor concerns, performing recharge administration and serving as PalCard holder, reconciler, and reviewer, and reconciling unrestricted and gift accounts. This position develops and maintains budgets and prepares financial reports for state and extramural funding, which may be complex, including stipend disbursement for research development and workforce training programs. This position participates in the development and revision of standard operating procedures and guidelines, serves as backup to pre-award processes, and assists with post-award monthly reconciling and documentation organization and storage. This position provides guidance to supervisors and managers in developing job descriptions and personnel policies and procedures, coordinates and participates in academic personnel and human resources activities including employment, training, and classification, serves as UCPath payroll initiator, and ensures completion of HR and Payroll forms and documentation for the unit/department. This position conducts trend analyses and helps develop resulting recommendations based on account reconciliation and spending patterns across unrestricted, gift, and program accounts, including research development and workforce training programs, and may assist with related fundraising activities.
Please Note: This is a hybrid position (3 days minimum onsite)
Ability to use sound judgment in responding to issues and concerns.
Working knowledge of research administration, including pre-award and post-award processes, documentation, stipend disbursement, and applicable requirements.
Solid communication and interpersonal skills to communicate effectively with all levels of staff verbally and in writing.
Solid organizational skills and ability to multi-task with demanding timeframes.
Sound judgment, discretion, and confidentiality, with working knowledge of UCPath and common financial, human resources, and office applications.
Ability to use discretion and maintain confidentiality.

Knowledge of administrative operations across finance, human resources and payroll, facilities and space, purchasing, communications and information technology, events, student services, and contracts and grants support.
Ability to reconcile accounts, prepare financial reports, analyze financial and human resources data, identify discrepancies and trends, and make recommendations.
Ability to coordinate human resources and payroll activities, develop procedures, maintain records, and support compliance with University, federal, and state requirements.

Strong organizational, communication, and project coordination skills to manage multiple priorities, support programs, events, and facilities needs, advise supervisors and managers, and oversee student assistants.
